label: rem:sl-n-color-frame-scope
title: Scope of the $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ frame
html:
Convention. A color observable is read with the framed generator \sigma_i^{\mathfrak{sl}} = q^{-1/N}\sigma_i of Proposition. Every other observable keeps the Hecke normalisation (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0. The rescaling is not applied to the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) or to the writhe-normalised Markov trace. A uniform rescaling would multiply an unnormalised trace \mathrm{tr}_M(w) by q^{-\mathrm{wr}(w)/N}, where \mathrm{wr}(w) is the writhe of the word w, and would send z to q^{-1/N} z. Words of writhe zero are unaffected; words of nonzero writhe are not, so the scope matters.

The two-strand color factors. In the Hecke normalisation the two exchange channels of 3 \otimes 3 = \bar 3 \oplus 6 have log-exponents \pm 1. Their ratio is 1, against the group-theoretic |c_{\bar 3}/c_6| = 2. In the \mathrm{SU}(3) frame the log-exponents are -\tfrac43 and \tfrac23, so the ratio is 2 with both signs correct.

What the factor 2 was. The identity \log|\lambda_{\mathrm{S}}| + \log|\lambda_{\mathrm{A}}| = 0 for the Hecke eigenvalues, i.e. |\det \sigma_i| = 1 on V \otimes V, is the statement that the \mathfrak{u}_1 summand of \mathfrak{gl}_N = \mathfrak{sl}_N \oplus \mathfrak{u}_1 shifts both exponents by the same 1/N. It is a normalisation of the generator, not a structural obstruction to the color sector.

The nuclear channel is not repaired. The same frame at N = 2 gives the channel ratio (N+1)/(N-1) = 3. The nuclear T = 0 / T = 1 ratio it would have to reproduce is \approx 33.7. So the color frame does not supply the missing nuclear mechanism. This is a scope-limited negative: it says that this frame alone does not reach 33.7, not that framing cannot enter a nuclear closure.
